answerability: partly: the file supports comparing motorist and cyclist deaths as each group's share of their combined recorded deaths in police-reported NYC crashes, but it does not establish each group's share of all NYC road deaths
metric: annual share of combined motorist-plus-cyclist deaths attributable to motorists and to cyclists
denominator: for each calendar year, the sum of motorist and cyclist deaths across crashes with both death counts present
population: police-reported NYC crash records dated 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31 with both motorist and cyclist death counts present; denominator includes only these two recorded road-user categories
filters: retain rows only when both number_of_motorist_killed and number_of_cyclist_killed are present
years: calendar years 2013 through 2025, grouped by year of crash_date
grouping: year, with separate series for motorist and cyclist shares

data_check.facts: There are 2,132,218 crash records in 2013-2025. In each year both death columns and crash_date have zero missing values, so the complete-pair rule excludes zero rows; all years have records and observed dates span January 1 through December 31. No selected row has crash_date 1900-01-01 or 1970-01-01.
data_check.decision: Keep all eligible rows and disclose that shares compare only these two road-user categories within police-reported crashes. There are no rows dropped or differently counted because of missing death counts, and no partial calendar years.

limitations: The denominator is only the recorded motorist and cyclist deaths, so the shares do not represent proportions of all road-user deaths; the file also has no exposure denominator such as population, trips, or distance traveled.
